sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: no-parking distances, hill parking, parallel parking steps, highway parking, belt exemptions, child seats, unattended people and pets, littering, crash duties, motorcycle insurance and registration
Confusable pairs from the parking, restraint, crash and insurance pages, followed by continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
The four no-parking distances on one list are 10 feet from a fire hydrant, 20 feet from a crosswalk at an intersection, 30 feet from a roadside flashing light, stop sign or signal, and 50 feet from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing. [A01]
Why it matters: group parking; confusable hydrant versus crosswalk versus signal versus rail; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
Keep watching through the rear window the whole time you back up rather than relying only on mirrors or a back-up camera, and back slowly into the closest lane. [A01]
Why it matters: group backing; links to the backing rules in part one.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
Parking is also banned on any bridge, inside a highway tunnel and across the street end of a driveway. [A01]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
Stopping on the traffic side of a vehicle already parked at a curb or highway edge is called double parking and is not allowed. [A01]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A01
You also may not park beside a yellow-painted curb, where official No Parking signs stand, next to or opposite an excavation or obstacle if you would block traffic, or in front of mailboxes where local rules forbid it. [A01]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A02
Downhill with or without a curb and uphill without a curb, the wheels turn toward the edge of the road; only uphill with a curb do they turn away from it. [A02]
Why it matters: group hill parking; confusable uphill with curb versus without; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A02
In the parallel parking steps you turn the wheel sharply right and back slowly, turn sharply left once clear of the car ahead while still backing, then turn sharply right and pull toward the curb in the middle of the space. [A02]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; prereq is the starting position beside the car ahead.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A03
On a state highway or freeway, move a parked vehicle off the main part of the road, and if it cannot be moved, put out visible markers or signals so other drivers are not harmed. [A03]
Why it matters: group highway parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A03
A vehicle parked on the highway should use parking lights or hazard warning lights to alert others, with any headlights set to low beam. [A03]
Why it matters: group highway parking; confusable parking lights versus low beam.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A03
As the driver you are responsible for every passenger's safety, so insist that everyone buckles up and that children ride in a restraint suited to their age. [A03]
Why it matters: group passenger safety; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A03
The seat belt is called the most important safety equipment in the vehicle, and it keeps occupants from being thrown out, which usually brings death or serious injury. [A03]
Why it matters: group seat belts; links to the airbag limits.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A03
Other belt exemptions cover a rural mail carrier delivering for the U.S. Postal Service, a person driving or riding in a pickup during farm work, and a vehicle built before Jan. 1, 1965. [A03]
Why it matters: group belt exemptions; confusable with the reverse, full-seat and doctor exemptions; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A03
Belt exemptions are narrow: a worker who gets in and out often loses the exemption above 25 mph, while a driver of a passenger vehicle is exempt only while backing up. [A03]
Why it matters: group belt exemptions; confusable speed-limited versus reverse-only exemption.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A04
Rear-facing is the rule for a child under 2 until the seat's limit is reached, while the booster stage covers children aged 4 to 9 who have outgrown their car seat. [A04]
Why it matters: group child seats; confusable rear-facing versus booster ages; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A04
If a child seat has no expiration date stamped on it, follow the six-year rule counted from the date it was made. [A04]
Why it matters: group child seats; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A04
Never put a rear-facing infant seat in front of an active airbag, never carry a child on a passenger's lap, and do not let children ride in the cargo area of a truck or station wagon. [A04]
Why it matters: group child seats; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A04
Never leave children or vulnerable adults alone in a vehicle, because they could set it in motion, face deadly heat or cold, be in a car that is stolen, or be harmed by someone breaking in. [A04]
Why it matters: group unattended occupants; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A04
To guard against theft, lock the doors, take the keys with you, never leave the engine running, and leave nothing that looks valuable in sight. [A04]
Why it matters: group unattended vehicle; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A05
Pets should not be left in a vehicle, especially on very hot or very cold days, because extreme temperatures can be very dangerous for animals. [A05]
Why it matters: group animals; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A05
The airbag page repeats, for safety reasons, that children under age 13 must ride in the back seat whenever one is available. [A05]
Why it matters: group airbags; repeated on the airbag page as the reason for the back seat rule.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A05
Move front passenger seats as far back as they go, and read the operator's manual before driving or riding in a vehicle with airbags. [A05]
Why it matters: group airbags; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A05
Throwing or dumping anything from a vehicle onto roads or public or private land is illegal, including cigarettes, fireworks, snow, ice, glass, nails, cans, garbage, ashes and animal carcasses. [A05]
Why it matters: group littering; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A05
A crash that hurts or kills someone requires a call to law enforcement or 911, while a property-damage-only crash needs no police notice, only towing if disabled and telling any other property owner. [A05]
Why it matters: group crash duties; confusable injury crash versus property-damage-only crash; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A06
Motorcycle drivers must carry liability coverage for property damage and injuries to others, while no-fault and uninsured driver coverage is optional for them. [A06]
Why it matters: group insurance; confusable motorcycle versus car coverage; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-R25 | anchor: A06
Running an uninsured vehicle can also cost the vehicle's license plates and registration, separate from any court penalty. [A06]
Why it matters: group insurance; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-R26 | anchor: A06
To register a vehicle, take its current title or registration card and your driver's license or other valid ID to the nearest deputy registrar's office. [A06]
Why it matters: group registration; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-R27 | anchor: A06
The insurance reinstatement fee is $30, while the repeat messaging fine is $275 and the uninsured-vehicle fine can reach $1,000. [A06]
Why it matters: group fines; confusable reinstatement fee versus fines; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]
